title: Obedience to the Word
definition: Obedience to the Word is the faithful response of trusting, submitting to, and practicing what God commands and teaches in Scripture.
summary: God's Word is not given merely to be admired, debated, or memorized. It is given to lead His people into faith, repentance, worship, holiness, love, endurance, and mission.
christFocus: Jesus perfectly obeyed the Father and calls His disciples to hear and keep His words by grace.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Obedience to the Word teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to obedience to the word by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
